stemMd: For x > 0 and x ≠ 1, what is logₓ(x³)?
explanationMd: By definition logₓ(x³) is the exponent to which x must be raised to produce x³, namely 3. The base restrictions x > 0 and x ≠ 1 make the real logarithm valid.

distractorRationale.d: The logarithm asks for an exponent, not the base.
distractorRationale.c: This multiplies the exponent and base incorrectly.
distractorRationale.a: This reports the argument rather than its logarithm.
distractorRationale.e: This would arise from reversing base and argument.
